01.title: OUT OF LIFE
01.tagline: the maze, the haze, the fall, the ember
01.logline: A poet reads aloud to a lover's turned back; the vape haze claims the room, the lover falls off the fire escape, and the poet falls behind — out of life — until it gets as dark as black.
01.thesis: The way out he searches for (hallways, drawers, fire escapes) is the way down; leaving is not an exit but a direction.

02.title: FLASHING LIGHTS
02.logline: Floating in black between caving walls, a poet's eyes dilate until the pupil swallows the frame — and inside is age six: a window, a winding road, arguing headlights, a ghost with a tambourine, and the first throw.
02.thesis: The silent scream and the silent call are the same instrument; the tambourine is the first time the poet answers noise with noise.

03.title: HOW TO BREAK OFF AN ENGAGEMENT
03.tagline: the storm takes everything that was ever called goods
03.logline: The tambourine thrown at age six flies into a chapel still whole, waits at the altar step through the cobwebs, and a time-lapse storm takes the building down to two stubs and a doorway — then the storm ends, the film turns white, and the tambourine falls one last time and shatters among two sets of footprints.
03.thesis: An engagement is broken the way a chapel decays: first the cross tilts, then the roof, then the register of the world itself — and the gift that started it all only breaks after everything it was thrown at is gone.

04.title: NEVERMORE
04.tagline: a trail followed twice, a vow made twice
symbols: Throbbing heart/Familiar heart/Reclaimed heart/Dusk settled heart
Moonlit night’s garden fields/Golden hue plants
carried: Moonlit night’s garden fields/Golden hue plants
Throbbing heart/Familiar heart/Reclaimed heart/Dusk settled heart
04.logline: In red and black, hands in pockets, a poet walks the shore of everything that broke, lets a heart lift itself back into his chest, follows the trail into a night that falls through the film's own register, and searches a bare field until his hands — they too used to be his — return, and the arms are drawn for the first time.
04.thesis: Recovery is not retrieval: the heart and the hands come back on their own terms, and the self's only work is to walk, kneel, and receive — nevermore said once per organ.

05.title: BLOODLINES
05.tagline: he names the stars after the people who made him
symbols: Deepening voice/Baritone of a million cries/Unanswered plight
dropped_symbols: Deepening voice/Baritone of a million cries/Unanswered plight
05.logline: Told NOW GO, the poet walks into a parade of crowned ancestors who hand him stars to name, lower a galaxy into his returned hands, hover his basement childhood in the sky as a white lit room, run their blood through his fingerprint whorls until his voice drops to a baritone of a million cries — and open marble gates with wings to welcome him through.
05.thesis: Inheritance is not received but conducted: the blood is an orchestra, the stars take new names, and the gates only open for a body that has already gotten its heart and hands back.

06.title: RESURRECTING ATLANTIS
06.tagline: a city comes up out of the water
06.logline: Down a road that lights its own bricks, past comets all pointing one way, the poet watches a drowned city let go of its water, pays the gate with one of his named stars, wanders streets where every joyful noise blooms a rainbow, stands in a plaza until the whole city blinks with his heart — and follows the music into a house.
06.thesis: A city born in unison out of the purest of fictions is entered the way faith is: you pay with something you were just given a name for, and the light at the door costs you your own.

07.title: DJ TURN ME UP
07.logline: A DJ is lowered into the house on a beam of light, the needle rings the room, and the poet — eyes wide shut, chin nested down — tells the whole love story over a rising fader: ghosts in vineyards, rings diverging, a home trucked apart, eleven petals plunked off a daisy, three roads and one silver lining — until the chin nests high and the volume clips.
07.thesis: Being heard is a gain structure: the same story at level one is grief and at level eight is testimony — the fader, not the words, is what turns forth to face delights and shadows.

08.title: NEWLY SINGLE
08.tagline: a soul leaves a body on a dance floor
08.logline: On a rooftop running faster than its own night, the poet's soul steps out of his body, watches all of Atlantis top-down, stands at the equator of a hotter planet, lets angels pour moon-salted ice baths over the husk he left dancing — then returns, leans back, breathes the whole room in, and at the railing holds a ring out over the edge and cannot let it go.
08.thesis: Separation is a frame-rate: the body grieves at the world's speed and the soul at its own — and what returns from the split is not relief but accuracy: what isn't mine, I still can not give.

09.title: YET, HEARD
09.logline: Through a fawning crowd, past a moon that runs its phases over one walk, into a phone booth twice — mother's living room arriving as an inset with a tear down its crease, father's footprints lighting under his son's feet — while the break-up widens in the background of every shot, until the EX dissolves to weather and a motorcycle blinks its lamp at the man left standing.
09.thesis: Farewell is not an event but a background process: it runs at its own rate behind every call, every walk, every prayer — and being heard does not stop it; it only means someone watched it happen with you.

10.title: MAGIC RIDE
10.tagline: night replaced by morning, dot by dot
10.logline: Not looking for a ride, he rubs his aggressions into the steel anyway — and one ride carries the whole film from black to white: through streets where heads twist twice, past loneliness shredded by his own noise, under a settling moon, across a grey hour where the frames themselves trade registers, into a believable morning that is chilly, and back to the shore where everything broke — arriving this time, not washing up.
10.thesis: The magic still existing is not an event but a direction: darkness is crossed at riding speed, the stars you were given come inside, and the same shore means something different when you choose to stop there.

11.title: NEW DAY
11.tagline: the temple assembles, one course at a time
11.logline: The fog exhales its introduction over the ruin, and the ruin answers by lifting itself: stones float into a new base course, the broken arch straightens into a doorway, a parabolic shell draws itself left to right — and when the water arrives edgeless, the temple learns to reflect, the poet walks the waterline with his own inversion underfoot, and the sun ends up overhead.
11.thesis: Catharsis is construction with the original materials: nothing new arrives — the same stones, the same arch, the same man — only the schedule runs the other way.

12.title: REUNION
12.tagline: less time for words, more space for laughter
12.logline: Decades later, inside the temple they rebuilt, three friends arrive through a door of light, trade their words in for laughter, go quiet for the crowned elders who stand faintly among them, flip the burning hourglass rather than let the occasion be one-time — and part ways trailing curls of wind, hearts still blinking in unison.
12.thesis: Brotherhood is a shared clock: the hug synchronizes it, the laughter funds it, the flip extends it — and the winds can part ways without breaking the tempo.

13.title: HOW TO WIN MY HEART
13.logline: At the harbor cafe he watches couples orbit like Jupiter's moons and elders clutch what they kept, while his own love stories sit char-eaten at his elbow — so he harvests the flowers into his power instead, until a distant lit window says YOU'LL SEE ME, and instead of leaving toward anything, he sets the bouquet on the rail and sits back down: don't make me leave; I escaped here for a reason.
13.thesis: Winning this heart is not pursuit but placement: stay where you escaped to, put the gathered power somewhere visible, and let the window keep its light on.

14.title: HOT MINUTE
14.tagline: everything learns to be weather, then a door
14.logline: The haze gathers on the water and takes everything he built — boats, cafe, her window gently, the flowers last — then takes him ground-up until only the pulse blinks in the black. What follows is the suite remembering itself in twelve flashes, a dance of two entwined muses around one center, and an old vintage door opening on a slow warm party: the kind he once fell out of a window to escape, and now walks into, from the back, at his own speed, as the door closes and keeps him.
14.thesis: Leaving and arriving are the same door seen from different registers: the suite opens with a fall out of a window and closes with a walk through a door — and the victory is not escaping the party, but choosing it.
